Back to index

What this is. Output of the SF++ set-reconciliation simulator in NomDeTom/Meshtasticatom, built from the run digests on its sim-results branch by a scheduled job. Nothing on this page is hand-written or hand-edited.

What it is not. Not a measurement of a real network. The radio model, terrain and clutter come from Meshtasticator and Komzpa's terrain stack; the mesh, traffic and archive behaviour are simulated. held and union are what an archive holds, not what a user receives.

Reading it. The four delivery measures have four different denominators and are not comparable to each other. demand is aggregate airtime demand across the whole mesh, a multiple with no ceiling; chutil is what a device reports and cannot exceed 100%.

Licence. This page is output of the simulator in NomDeTom/Meshtasticatom, which is distributed under GPL-3.0 because parts of it are transcribed from Meshtastic firmware. A program's output is not the program: this page describes a simulation and is free to read and quote. The simulator's Meshtasticator half remains CC BY 4.0, attribution preserved. Part of that simulator's source is based on Spinsante, Gioacchini and Scalise, A novel experimental-based tool for the design of LoRa networks (MetroInd4.0&IoT, 2019), which stems from Bor, Roedig, Voigt and Alonso, Do LoRa Low-Power Wide-Area Networks Scale? (MSWiM '16) and the LoRaSim library. Terrain, clutter and the capture-aware physics are from Komzpa's Meshtasticator branch.

What moves a delivery measure

Mean spread of the measure each block moves most, averaged over the runs that carry it. The four measures have four denominators and are not comparable to each other - measure names which one this block travels in. A large text spread beside it means the block decides its measure by spending the mesh's own broadcast reach.

Schedule

Every cell the tree declares, against the runs in this archive. Two different readings of “still to do” and they disagree by design: the block sweep runs nightly and touches all 87 every night, while the matrix and the cross run weekly and touch a cell once a week - so not in the latest run means something for the first and nothing for the other two. runs counts every run a cell appears in; never is the column that means work outstanding.

cellrunslast runlatestcovers
AD-amplifiers5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noPower amplifiers as separate transmit and receive gain, sprinkled or in an arms race.
AD-amplify-worst5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noA high amplifier fitted to the worst-connected nodes after the links exist - the field pathology where the node nobody could hear is then heard by everyone while still hearing almost nobody.
AD-badrouters5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhere the router roles land - on the best-connected nodes, the worst, or at random.
AD-flooding5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noEvery node rebroadcasting everything, against a real role census.
AD-nomute5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe role census: a real mesh's mix, the same without muted clients, and everything a router.
AD-siting5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSiting against a real role census, including a basement-heavy mesh.
AD-worst5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noRouter roles on the worst-connected nodes of an already badly sited mesh - the adversarial case.
BL-control5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same nodes in the same places with the archive off then on, separating what serving costs a node from where it sits.
DB-hotstore5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe modelled MAX_NUM_NODES - the size of the hot store.
DB-hotstore-stress5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe store size against a fixed 250-node mesh, so eviction is constant.
DB-platform5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe board mix, which decides each node's hot-store size.
DB-warm5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe warm tier on a mesh larger than the hot store: 0 is the pre-2.8 behaviour of forgetting an evicted peer outright.
DG-burst5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same nominal loss delivered in 60-second stretches of deafness, which puts a whole bucket's divergence into one sketch instead of spreading it.
DG-loss5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noA flat loss floor on every reception - degradation spread evenly across every bucket.
DG-outage5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noBurst loss at half an hour rather than a minute - most of a bucket, which is the outage that actually matters to an archive.
DM-mode5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow a DM escalates to flooding.
FW-firmware5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe pre-fold-in transport against 2.8 - same seed, same mesh, only the MAC and routing rules change.
FW-mixed5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noA mesh part-way through upgrading, the older share on 2.5.
FW-mixed-265blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same with the older share on 2.6.
FW-signing-cost5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSigning itself, on against off inside 2.8. The only arm that separates 'signing costs reach' from '2.8 costs reach'.
FW-versions5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe release series in order, each at its final release - what a mesh gained or lost per upgrade, not what one rule is worth.
LD-chatty5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe device broadcast interval driven down to three times its default rate.
LD-chatty-hops5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same, with every node on a flat hop limit of 7 so nothing damps the flood.
LD-diurnal5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noTime of day. Text, position and DMs follow the clock; telemetry and nodeinfo are device timers and do not.
LD-interval5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe device broadcast interval - the denominator every SF++ airtime share is quoted against.
LD-traceroute5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noRoute discoveries per node per hour - whether traceroute learning pays for its own airtime.
LD-traceroute-small5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same on a mesh whose hot store cannot hold it, where the overflow cache is all that keeps a route for the long tail.
MS-density5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same node counts in a fixed area, so this is density rather than size. Running both is the only way to say which an effect belongs to.
MS-hopscale5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow far the firmware's hop estimator sits from the exhaustive count it approximates, as the mesh outgrows its 128 entries.
MS-oversubscribed5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noMesh size against a store that has to hold it, over a full day.
MS-roles5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe legacy default role census against a real mesh's.
MS-roles-fav5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same with router favourites on.
MS-router-late5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe share of nodes on ROUTER_LATE.
MS-siting5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhere nodes physically are. A roof node and a basement one are 26 dB apart, wider than most parameters here.
MS-size5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noMesh size with density held constant - the area grows with the node count.
MS-stretch5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noEvery distance scaled about the centroid: the same nodes in the same arrangement, further apart.
MS-topology5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe shape of the mesh, at fixed node count and seed.
PR-crladder5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noRaising the coding rate on each retransmission - airtime spent to make each attempt likelier to land.
PR-dmmode-cr5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noDM escalation with the coding-rate ladder already on, since both spend the same retry budget.
PR-protocol5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noNothing, the incumbent chain walk, and the sketch - with `none` a paired baseline, so every other cell is a difference rather than a comparison.
PR-repeats5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe cheapest rival to an archive: one extra relay of a text rather than replicating it afterwards.
PR-repeats-busy5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same, on a mesh busy enough for the suppression thresholds to be deciding it.
RF-bw5005blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSpreading factor with bandwidth held at 500 kHz, where North America is heading.
RF-duct5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noTropospheric ducting episodes per hour. Not a free gain - read ducted receptions beside collisions.
RF-eu-presets5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe presets Europe runs, including the narrow ones EU_866 and EU_N_868 default to.
RF-noise5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe noise floor: none, a smooth field, episodic bursts, or a regular emitter that wipes whatever is in flight.
RF-preset5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe presets deployed meshes actually run: the default, the fast end, and the slow end still in use.
RF-preset-turbo1blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noPresets from the fastest the firmware ships to the slow end.
RF-pulse5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow often the periodic emitter fires.
RF-stretch-duct5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noDucting on a stretched mesh, where the long links it creates are the ones that were missing.
RF-txpower5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noTransmit power in dBm - the region limit is a ceiling an operator may use, not one they must.
RT-adopt5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe hop-recommendation feedback loop closed against held open, traced, because a converged mean and an oscillating one look identical at the end.
RT-favourites5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noRouter-like nodes favouriting each other, so relays between them keep their hop limit.
RT-hopassign5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhether raised hop limits land on central nodes as operators do it, or at random - the control that separates the limit's effect from the siting of the nodes that raised it.
RT-hoplimit5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHop limits past anything a release ships, to find where more hops stop helping.
RT-hopspread5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noOne hop limit for everyone, swept. The per-node spread must be off or --hop-limit is never read.
RT-rebroadcast5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe rebroadcast mode - what a node relays.
RT-spread5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noA uniform hop limit against per-node limits of 3-7 assigned by centrality.
SC-signing5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe receive-side signature policy - what a node does with an unsigned packet.
SF-advert-transport5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhether an archive advertises by broadcast or by DM to each known peer.
SF-bucket-mode5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhat defines a bucket: a global counter (a fiction kept as an upper bound), the local count the firmware keeps, a time window, or a sliding window.
SF-bucket-time5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWidth of the time bucket, when buckets are cut by the clock.
SF-cadence5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhen an archive advertises: on a sealed bucket, a fixed interval, AIMD, or both.
SF-capacity5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow many differences one sketch can decode before it fails and the exchange escalates.
SF-capacity-local5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSketch capacity under local numbering and the later defaults.
SF-capacity-window5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSketch capacity under windowed buckets rather than counted ones.
SF-catchup5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe quiet-hours window reconciliation defers to, which only means anything once traffic has a time of day.
SF-hops-flat5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow many hops apart the archives are placed, under a flat hop limit.
SF-hops-spread5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow many hops apart the archives are, under real per-node hop limits.
SF-jitter-global5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSpread applied to bucket-close under global numbering, where every archive seals the same bucket at the same moment and fires together.
SF-jitter-local5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noAdvert spread under local numbering, where each archive seals its own bucket on its own count and the synchronisation jitter would break is largely absent.
SF-place-flat5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhere the archives sit, under a flat hop limit.
SF-place-spread5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhere the archives sit, under real per-node hop limits.
SF-provide-transport5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhether a replay goes by DM or by broadcast, so bystanders in earshot can file it too.
SF-replay-order5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhere a replayed object lands in the receiver's stream: at the tip, or back at its heard_ago.
SF-replay-order-broadcast5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe same, with replays broadcast - the combination the replay header exists for.
SF-resolve5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow two archives settle a disagreement - send a sketch, enumerate, or sketch then fall back. Delivery should not move; what it costs should.
SF-servers-allrouters5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noEvery router as an archive against half of them - same mesh, same traffic, only who holds the archive changes.
SF-servers-flat5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow many archives the mesh has, under a flat hop limit.
SF-servers-spread5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noHow many archives the mesh has, under real per-node hop limits.
SF-signed5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhether the advert carries its 66-byte signature.
SF-sr-retries5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noRetries per addressed reconciliation hop, to find where delivery stops improving.
SF-width5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noSketch member width. Narrower identifiers collide more often, and a collision cancels in the sketch without cancelling in the checksum.
SF-window-size5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noObjects in the sliding window, when buckets are windowed.
TH-congestion5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noThe firmware's node-count interval scaling, on against off.
TH-congestion-input5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noWhich quantity drives the throttle: what the firmware can see and which saturates, or the unbounded ideal.
TH-congestion-mode5blocks-2026-08-26-7218105noEach node throttling on its own online count against one coefficient for the whole mesh. The firmware does the former.

batumi-coding-rate-ladder1design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; each retransmission goes out at a higher coding rate - more redundancy and more airtime per attempt. Not in any release. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-congestion-401design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; broadcast intervals still start stretching above 40 nodes, the firmware's own constant. This arm must reproduce the unchanged mesh exactly. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-congestion-601design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; broadcast intervals hold their shipped cadence up to 60 nodes before stretching, so the mesh stays chattier for longer. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-congestion-801design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; broadcast intervals hold their shipped cadence up to 80 nodes - on a mesh this size, almost no throttling at all. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-extra-repeats1design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; a node tolerates a second heard copy before cancelling its own rebroadcast, so a text is relayed more often. Not in any release. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-favourite-routers1design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; router-like nodes favourite each other, so a relay between two of them keeps its hop limit instead of spending one. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-hop-limit-151design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; every node at 15 hops - a ceiling far past anything this mesh can use, which is the point: it shows what the limit was costing when it bound. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-hop-limit-71design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; every node at 7 hops instead of the per-node 3-7 by centrality. Also removes the centrality assignment, so it is two changes and reads as one. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.
batumi-hop-scaling-401design-2026-08-25-8765439nothe 92-node Batumi snapshot on its own ground, at the shipped defaults; the hop recommendation still aims at 40 nodes, the firmware's own constant. This arm must reproduce the unchanged mesh exactly. Crossed against the archive off and at every placement and count.

Run health

What each run cost and what it flagged. Duration is given both ways on purpose. compute h is what the run actually spent, which is what decides whether a job fits its ceiling; s/sim-h is wall-clock seconds per simulated hour, the only form comparable between runs of different length - and the form the digest gates on, because the total moves whenever --hours or the seed count does. Flag kinds are counted, not ranked: beyond-envelope on a mirrored cell is expected by construction, and colouring every warning red would train everyone to skip them.

How these runs are made

Everything here is written by scheduled workflows into one archive branch, and this page is rebuilt from that archive. They ask two different kinds of question, which is why one block list holds two naming conventions: a synthetic mesh moving one flag at a time, and a real mesh over real ground.

1. The mechanism sweep

synthetic meshnightly 02:10 UTCruns/blocks-<date>-<seed>

What does this one variable do to a mesh? Every block sfpp.sweep declares - 87 of them - against a generated mesh, with one landform and one seed base drawn for the whole night so every block that night saw the same draw. One arm moves per block; everything else is held. Each block is its own job, because a single job running all 87 in sequence is about six hours of simulator time and one slow block would take the night down with it.

Cells are named <DD>-subject - a two-letter domain and a kebab tail, RF-preset-turbo, SF-capacity, DG-outage. The archive is switched on in every cell, so this style can say what a variable does and can never say what the archive itself is worth.

2. Real ground

Batumi, real geometry and terraintwo workflowsruns/matrix-<date>, runs/design-<date>-<seed>

Both run over a real node snapshot with matching terrain, so their cells are named for the ground rather than a domain: batumi-x1-LONG_FAST, batumi-coding-rate-ladder - scenario, mirror count, then the thing being varied. They predate the domain scheme and are not governed by it.

They are heavier than the mechanism sweep: the link build is O(n²) with a terrain profile and a clutter walk per pair, so a mirrored cell spends most of its time before the simulation starts. Neither runs its whole grid nightly - each night takes the stalest cells it has not covered recently, so a full pass completes over roughly a week.

Sim Sweep (matrix) · 03:40 UTC · three presets, two scales, three placements, three archive counts, five seeds, with a no-archive baseline per seed per scale. Asks whether a preset ordering survives scaling, and whether any deliberate placement beats picking nodes at random.

Sim Design (cross) · 04:40 UTC · a three-axis cross: what the archive is configured as, against what could be deployed instead of it, on each mesh in the round. This is the one that can answer what the archive is worth, because the archive sits on an axis rather than being on everywhere.

What joins them up

Sim Collate is called by all three rather than scheduled. It reduces a run to the two files this page reads - summary.json and trend.md - and applies the standing gates, so a run that produced an impossible number is caught where it was made.

Sim Results Explorer rebuilds this page at 06:20 UTC, after all three producers have finished. It reads only the digests, never the raw block JSONs, so the archive can drop raw runs without the page losing its history - and a figure that lives beside a dropped JSON can never be shown here at all, which is why the charts are drawn in the browser from numbers embedded in the page.
